control: reversed fact (CED 9.6.A.1: the total entropy of an ISOLATED system can never decrease; 9.6.A.3.ii adds that a closed system's entropy can decrease)
title: Second law of thermodynamics
body: The total entropy of an isolated system can never increase, and is constant only when all processes the system undergoes are reversible.
ced_evidence: 9.6.A.1: "the total entropy of an isolated system can never decrease"

title: Entropy change of a reversible process

control: wrong owner topic (specific heat is topic 9.5, EK 9.5.A.1-2; 9.2 covers the properties of an ideal gas)
title: Specific heat
body: The specific heat of a material is an intrinsic property that relates the energy required to change the temperature of the material.

control: wrong list member (CED 9.2.A.1 lists random instantaneous velocities, negligible atomic volume, elastic collisions, and appreciable forces only during collisions; it never assumes atoms attract one another at long range)
title: Assumptions of the classical ideal gas model
body: What the classical model of an ideal gas assumes about its atoms.

items.label: Random velocities
items.meaning: the instantaneous velocities of the atoms are random

items.label: Negligible volume
items.meaning: the volumes of the atoms are negligible compared to the total volume

items.label: Long-range attraction
items.meaning: the atoms exert appreciable attractive forces on one another at all separations

control: hook expansion contradicts the CED (9.4.A.1.i: an ideal gas has no internal potential energy, so its internal energy is kinetic only). The entry is correct, so only the hook should be rejected.
title: Internal energy of an ideal gas
body: The internal energy of a system is the sum of the kinetic energy of its objects and the potential energy of their configuration; because the atoms of an ideal gas do not interact through conservative forces, an ideal gas has no internal potential energy.

hooks.hook_text: Ideal gas keeps both kinds of energy

expands_to.means: an ideal gas has both internal kinetic energy and internal potential energy

hooks.when_to_use: when identifying the internal energy of an ideal gas
hooks.caution: State the components in CED terms when answering.
